title: Order lines with order details
prompt: The returns desk looks up order lines and needs each one with its order's date and status. Write `solve(order_items, orders)` so it returns `order_id`, `line_no`, `order_date`, `status`, `product_id` and `quantity`.
rules: Match a line to the order with the same `order_id`. Every line appears exactly once.
`orders` sometimes holds an exact copy of an order row, delivered twice by the load. A copy must not repeat its lines.
A line whose order isn't in `orders` still appears, with `order_date` and `status` missing. Orders with no lines are not listed. Return only these six columns, in this order.
hints: Every line must appear, so `order_items` is the side to keep whole: a left join from `order_items`.
A join pairs a line with every matching order row. If the same order row is there twice, the line comes out twice.
Remove the exact copies from `orders` with `distinct()` before joining. Don't use `distinct()` on the result: two identical order lines are both real.
explanation: Keep every line with a left join from `order_items`, after removing the copies from the other side: `order_items.join(orders.distinct(), on="order_id", how="left")`, then select the six columns. A join returns one row per matching pair, so an order row delivered twice would double every line of that order. `distinct()` on `orders` removes exact copies before they can multiply anything. Calling `distinct()` on the joined result instead looks similar but also merges two genuinely identical lines in `order_items`. Lines with an unknown order keep their row, with NULL date and status, which an inner join would drop.
